title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees in all axes and a translation vector also set to zero. On the first face, draw a single circle as the first loop. Place the center of this circle at coordinates (0.0304, 0.0304) and set the radius to 0.0304. Scale the entire 2D sketch by a factor of 0.0608. Ensure that the transformation maintains the original orientation and position by applying the same Euler angles and translation vector used initially. Extrude the scaled 2D sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units, creating a new solid body. The final dimensions of the cylindrical object will be a length of 0.06083618619385826, a width of 0.06083618619385826, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a circle in the sketch
r = r.center(0.0304, 0.0304).circle(0.0304)

# Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Scale the sketch (this step is not necessary as the scale is applied to the sketch before extrusion)
# r = r.scale(0.0608)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · best of 8
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0304, 0.0304)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0304)  # Draw a circle with the specified radius
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = (
    sketch
    .extrude(0.75)  # Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder
